description: Find pairs of customer rows sharing the same email, without ever pairing a row with itself and without listing the same pair twice in mirrored order
prompts: dup_pairs.sql is supposed to find pairs of customers who share the same email (a sign of accidental duplicate signups), returning (email, id_a, id_b) with id_a < id_b so each pair appears exactly once. The current query self-joins on email with `a.id != b.id`, which is wrong in two ways: it matches EVERY row to itself as well when the join has no other row to pair with (a row's own email always equals its own email, so with != it should exclude self-pairs, but it fails to guarantee id_a < id_b, so the SAME pair shows up TWICE, once as (id_a, id_b) and once as (id_b, id_a)). Fix the join condition to `a.id < b.id` instead of `a.id != b.id` so self-pairs are excluded AND each real pair appears exactly once, with id_a always the smaller id.

setup_files.dup_pairs.sql:
-- BUG: a.id != b.id excludes self-pairs but does not prevent each real
-- pair from appearing twice, once in each order.
SELECT a.email, a.id AS id_a, b.id AS id_b
FROM customers a
JOIN customers b ON a.email = b.email AND a.id != b.id
ORDER BY a.email, id_a, id_b;

reference_solution.dup_pairs.sql:
SELECT a.email, a.id AS id_a, b.id AS id_b
FROM customers a
JOIN customers b ON a.email = b.email AND a.id < b.id
ORDER BY a.email, id_a, id_b;

files.dup_pairs.sql:
SELECT a.email, a.id AS id_a, b.id AS id_b
FROM customers a
JOIN customers b ON a.email = b.email AND a.id != b.id
ORDER BY a.email, id_a, id_b;

name: add_sql_self_join_duplicate_email_pairs

test_setup_files.check_dup_pairs.py:
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path

sql = Path("dup_pairs.sql").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.executescript("""
CREATE TABLE customers (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL);
INSERT INTO customers VALUES
  (1, 'ada@example.com'),
  (2, 'grace@example.com'),
  (3, 'ada@example.com'),
  (4, 'ada@example.com');
""")

cur = con.execute(sql)
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
rows = cur.fetchall()

assert cols == ["email", "id_a", "id_b"], f"column names/order changed: {cols}"

# ada@example.com has 3 rows (1,3,4) -> pairs (1,3), (1,4), (3,4), each exactly once
expected = [
    ("ada@example.com", 1, 3),
    ("ada@example.com", 1, 4),
    ("ada@example.com", 3, 4),
]
assert rows == expected, f"expected: {expected}\ngot: {rows}"

print("PASS dup_pairs.sql behavior checks")
